plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the winter landscape of Japan. Their rose-like blooms open in deep crimson, soft pink or snowy white, with golden stamens at the center. They appear on branch tips while most other plants are dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Wild populations flower roughly January to March, so January 10 falls at the start of the season.
plants.location: Coastal woodlands and gardens of Japan, including southern Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close cousin of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan it has long been planted around shrines and temples.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: This low, leathery-leaved perennial pushes up nodding, cup-shaped white flowers in the cold of midwinter. As the blooms age, they blush pink. They are a welcome sight in woodland gardens when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Usually in flower by late December or early January in temperate gardens, and it carries on into late winter.
plants.location: Temperate woodland gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, such as the southeastern United States. It is native to the mountains of central and southern Europe.
plants.funFact: Despite the name, the Christmas Rose is not a rose. It belongs to the buttercup family, and every part of the plant is toxic.

plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.description: This Australian native shrub is covered in tiny white flowers in early summer. After the petals fall, the calyces swell and turn a vivid rose-red. The result is a festive, blooming-then-blushing display in the Southern Hemisphere summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Flowers from about November through January in the Southern Hemisphere, so it covers January 10.
plants.location: Coastal and sandstone bushland of New South Wales, Australia, and gardens in the same climate zone
plants.funFact: The red color that people take for petals comes from the enlarged sepals. This is why the plant has long been used as an Australian Christmas decoration.
